[34mInvestigated:[0m The Scheduler class and module-level wrappers in schedule/__init__.py, including run_pending, run_all, get_jobs, Job.should_run, and Job.run. Existing test_schedule.py structure and the pytest setup. The docs in docs/reference.rst and docs/examples.rst.

[33mLearned:[0m Job.should_run gates only run_pending, while run_all calls _run_job directly and Job.run has no pause check. A pause check therefore has to sit in run_pending to take effect, and run_all ignores pauses by design. A paused job's next_run is not advanced, so a job whose run time passed during the pause fires once on the first run_pending after resume.

[32mCompleted:[0m Scheduler.pause(tag) and Scheduler.resume(tag) are implemented, backed by a set of paused tags. run_pending skips any job carrying a paused tag, and pausing covers jobs tagged after the pause. Resuming an unpaused tag is a no-op. Module-level schedule.pause() and schedule.resume() wrappers were added, matching clear(tag). Five new tests were added to test_schedule.py, and the full suite passes at 88 tests. docs/reference.rst and docs/examples.rst were updated. Nothing has been committed.

[35mNext Steps:[0m The session is waiting on the user's decisions: whether pause and resume should stay module-level or become Scheduler-only, and whether a resumed job should reschedule from the resume time instead of firing once for missed runs. Committing the change is the likely next step once those are settled.

[36mNotes:[0m The module-level wrappers were added even though get_jobs_for was narrowed to Scheduler-only earlier in the session, so the two APIs are now inconsistent. No test currently asserts that run_all ignores paused tags, although the docstring states it.
